To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the participants in our study did not have a clear mental model of the functions of the video tool.

(a) the cognitive representation of tool functions is a necessary condition for the use of a technology in a pedagogical context; (b) cognitive representation of tool specific functions is necessary for the design of a technology based lesson plan; (c) cognitive representation of socio cognitive functions is a necessary and sufficient condition for the evaluation of a technology based teaching unit; and, (d) cognitive representation of technology affordances is necessary for the evaluation and design, but not for the use of video technologies

(a) the mental models of the participants did not include specific functions of WebDIVER(tm), and (b) participants' mental models of cognitive and socio cognitive tool functions differentially influenced lesson plan design and evaluation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question, how can pre service teachers be supported to develop TPCK for video technologies in history and language classes?
the question of how to support teachers in the development of TPCK.
how pre service teachers represent video tools in their mental model of TPCK.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the mental models of the participants were not sufficient to design and evaluate lesson plans that fully exploited the potentials of video tools for teaching and learning.
the more pre service teachers cognitively represented the tool functions, the more they were able to design a lesson plan that reflected the potential of the video tool.
pre service teachers' knowledge about video tools is a necessary but not a sufficient prerequisite for the design of effective lesson plans.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pre service teachers need to be supported to develop mental models of technology affordance that reflect the cognitive and socio cognitive functions of the technology.
the mental models of technology affordance are not only an indicator of how teachers use technology but also a predictor of how teachers design lessons.
pre service teachers should be provided with the opportunity to develop their own mental models of technology affordance.
The main takeaway from our work is that

pre service teachers need to understand that video technology is an instructional tool that can be employed in a variety of ways and that they need to be aware that they can use it to support their own learning.
pre service teachers need to be able to cognitively represent both technological and pedagogic knowledge in an integrated way to develop TPCK.
pre service teachers' TPCK development requires a focus on the interrelation between technological and pedagogically relevant functions of video tools.
